scope: Synthetic Reed Camp at fictional Greywater Reach; not a historical rule or universal Rise profile.

counting.unit: One permanent building or one distinct committed new-building project at this settlement, counted once.
includes: admitted new-building projects whether active or paused
cancelled projects with retained physical works
excludes: ordinary repairs to the same building
counting.completion: Atomically replace the completed project's reservation with its building; total usage does not change.
counting.last_slot: Admission and reservation are atomic across actors and retries; at most one competing project obtains the last slot.
counting.cancellation: Before work, an explicitly accepted cancellation releases the reservation and returns the two unspent project timber atomically. After work begins, cancellation retains the occupied place and physical works; disposition requires a separate reviewed contract.

prerequisites: issuer is active and authorized for this settlement
request is within this fictional jurisdiction
the recorded site review permits one further building place
authority.decision: If any prerequisite fails, record a refusal; otherwise issue an offer of exactly one additional place. A request or offer alone changes no allowance.
authority.terms: No fee, resource transfer, new land right, automatic approval, obligation or extra labor is implied. The founder must separately accept the unexpired offer; the effective grant changes the allowance exactly once.
authority.validity: A wrong-site, expired or revoked authority cannot create a valid offer or grant. Later changes do not erase existing buildings or receipts.

state_and_recovery.owner: Existing authoritative Core and applicable rights/work records; this document does not create a second state owner.
state_and_recovery.revalidation: At commit recheck issuer, site, current permission, allowance, physical fit and relevant resources.
state_and_recovery.failure: A rejected build or grant changes no materials, commitments, allowance or elapsed work.
state_and_recovery.retry: A repeated committed request returns its original actor-scoped result, without a second effect; restore fencing follows the Engine's eventual published contract.
state_and_recovery.migration: Existing saves must not receive an inferred allowance or silent rewrite; Engine must define an explicit migration and compatibility policy.

coordination.engine: Engine must review the terms and publish its state, API, actor-scoped receipt, durability and migration contracts before executable consumers.
coordination.app: App must consume only a reviewed, explicitly selected Engine/Catalog set; this proposal is not a launch or display authorization.
coordination.catalog: Catalog owns the fictional proposal and independent expectations; evaluator truth is not actor input.
